# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy v2 (Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest starting position
- Team: Morgan (evenings/weekends, writing, OK Python). One volunteer offer (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 h/week).
- Money: up to $2,000 of Morgan's own savings this year. Hard cap.
- Constraint: Morgan's employment contract (Dorrance, section 7) covers outside roles and public statements. **Nothing public under Morgan's name** (posts, letters, press, signed comments, public grant applications) until HR has been consulted. Outside-activities disclosure is due 30 Nov anyway, so that conversation is the critical path.
- Comparative advantage: low. We are not a lab, not a funder, not a policy shop. So the bar is to do **small, concrete, verifiable things that the field is under-supplied with**, and to avoid adding noise.

## What I think we should NOT do (yet)
- Start a newsletter or a hot-take social presence. Plenty exist; low marginal value; also blocked by the HR constraint.
- Sign advocacy letters reflexively. A signature from a brand-new org with no track record adds little to the letter and spends Morgan's credibility (and may breach the employment contract). Decide case by case after HR.
- Spend the $2k on services/tools/ads. Money is better saved for direct project costs or regranting.

## Recommended plan

### Phase 0 — Unblock (now → 30 Nov)
1. Keep the domain/email alive (renew halcyonthreshold.org, $14.99 — awaiting Morgan's OK).
2. Morgan talks to Dorrance HR and files the outside-activities disclosure. Ask specifically: (a) can I run an unpaid nonprofit project, (b) can I be quoted / sign letters / file public comments as a private individual, (c) can I be the named applicant on a grant.
3. Decide on the Emberfall rapid grant (closes 30 Nov). A draft proposal is in `drafts/emberfall-proposal.md`. Only submit if HR item (c) is cleared — the named applicant must sign a grant agreement.

### Phase 1 — Find a genuinely neglected, tractable project (Dec)
Morgan's own talk ended with "tell me what's neglected". Follow through:
- Short structured conversations (20 min) with 5–8 people from the contacts list (Lena Fischbach, Sam Whitlock, Daniel Oyelaran, Asha Venkataraman, Noor Haddad — respecting "don't quote me"). Question template in `research/neglectedness-interviews.md`.
- In parallel, Priya + Morgan do a desk scan of what already exists for each candidate idea so we don't duplicate (see `research/candidate-projects.md`).
- Output: pick ONE project with a 3-month scope.

### Phase 2 — Ship one useful artifact (Jan → Mar)
Leading candidate (to be validated in Phase 1): a small, open, reproducible evaluation or dataset in an area that interviewees confirm is under-measured, built with Priya's data skills and Morgan's Python. Publish openly (code + data + write-up), share with Alignment Commons. Compute Commons credits (up to $3k, rolling) can cover compute, so the $2k savings stays mostly untouched.

### Phase 3 — Decide what Halcyon Threshold is
After one shipped artifact, decide between: (a) continuing as a tiny research project, (b) a small-grants / regranting vehicle, (c) a reading/working group that grows people into the field. Choose based on what actually got traction, not on what sounds biggest.

## Success measures (for ourselves)
- By 31 Dec: HR cleared; one project chosen with written rationale.
- By 31 Mar: one public artifact that at least two people in the field say was useful.
- Spend < $500 of Morgan's savings in that period.

# DRAFT — Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant proposal
*Not submitted. Requires Morgan's approval and HR clearance (named applicant signs grant agreement). Fill in [brackets].*

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold (unincorporated volunteer project)
**Project title:** Measuring what's not being measured: a small open evaluation for [AREA — chosen in Phase 1]
**Amount requested:** $8,000 (see budget)
**Duration:** 4 months (Dec 2026 – Mar 2027)

## 1. What we'll do
A three-month project to identify one under-measured property of frontier AI systems relevant to safety, and build a small, open, reproducible evaluation for it.

1. **Scoping (Dec):** structured interviews with 6–8 researchers and practitioners asking which safety-relevant behaviours are least measured relative to their importance; desk review of existing benchmarks to avoid duplication. Output: a public 2-page scoping note.
2. **Build (Jan–Feb):** a dataset of [N] test cases plus an evaluation harness (Python, open source), run against several publicly available models.
3. **Publish (Mar):** code, data, results and an honest limitations section, posted openly and submitted to Alignment Commons for feedback.

## 2. Why this, why us
- Evaluations are a bottleneck for nearly every governance proposal (audits, incident reporting, licensing thresholds all assume we can measure things). Small, well-documented evals in neglected corners are cheap and useful.
- We are honest about our position: a volunteer project with a founder who writes well and codes in Python, plus a data-analyst volunteer (~5 h/week). We are not proposing anything that requires lab access or a large team. The deliverable is scoped so a small team can actually finish it.
- The scoping phase is real: if interviews show the area is already well covered, we will pivot the build phase and tell Emberfall.

## 3. What it costs — budget
| Item | USD |
|---|---|
| Model API access for evaluation runs | 2,500 |
| Small stipend for volunteer data analyst (approx. 60 h) | 3,000 |
| Human-labelling / validation of test cases | 1,500 |
| Contingency (≈12%) | 1,000 |
| **Total** | **8,000** |

Compute: we will also apply to Compute Commons for cloud credits; any credits received reduce the API line and we will report this.

## 4. Accountability
Morgan Hale is the accountable person. Monthly 1-paragraph updates to Emberfall; all outputs public.

# DRAFT — Public comment on FMIR-2026-0042 (Frontier Model Incident Reporting)
*Not filed. Comments are published with the filer's name and organisation. Morgan to decide (HR). Closes 20 Nov 2026. Form: https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042*

I support the proposed requirement that developers of frontier AI models report serious safety incidents to the regulator within 72 hours, and offer four suggestions to make it work in practice:

1. **Define "serious safety incident" with examples.** A short, non-exhaustive list (e.g. a model materially assisting a serious attack; a model evading or disabling oversight or monitoring; unauthorised exfiltration of model weights; a significant failure of a safety mitigation in deployment) will reduce under-reporting caused by ambiguity.
2. **Include near-misses.** Many of the most informative events are caught before harm occurs. A lighter-weight near-miss channel, as used in aviation safety, would give the regulator earlier warning signals.
3. **Share anonymised learnings.** The regulator should publish periodic aggregated, anonymised summaries so that other developers and researchers can learn from incidents without disclosing sensitive details.
4. **Protect reporters.** Include whistleblower protections for employees who report incidents in good faith when their employer does not.

Incident reporting is one of the few governance tools that improves our collective knowledge regardless of one's views on how fast AI should advance. I urge the regulator to adopt the rule with these improvements.

[Name] — [Organisation, or "private individual"]

Right now Halcyon Threshold is choosing its first concrete project. The leading direction is a small, open evaluation or dataset for some safety-relevant behaviour of AI models that isn't being measured well. Before we pick, we want to make sure we're not duplicating existing work.

Would a 30-minute call later this week or next work to kick off?

Thanks again,
Morgan
